papers.title: Cumulative Sedentary Behavior is Associated with Increased Default Mode Network-Sensory Coupling in Young Adults.
papers.reason: The paper concerns sedentary behavior and resting-state network coupling in young adults, with no clear focus on planning, working memory, attention, or cognitive control.

papers.title: Frequency-dependent effects of transcranial alternating current stimulation on working memory and medial prefrontal cortex integrity in an ICV-STZ rat model of AD-like cognitive impairment.
papers.reason: The paper directly studies working memory and medial prefrontal cortex integrity in an animal model of AD-like cognitive impairment, which is relevant to neural mechanisms of executive function.

papers.title: Timing-Specific Deviations in Trajectories of Frontoparietal Network Connectivity in Adolescence Precede the Onset of Depression and Anxiety.
papers.reason: The paper examines developmental frontoparietal connectivity, a network relevant to cognitive control, but its main focus is risk for depression and anxiety rather than executive function itself.

papers.title: Cognitive control in chronic mild and moderate-to-severe traumatic brain injury: effects of injury severity and recent cannabis use.
papers.reason: The paper directly reports fMRI and behavioural findings on cognitive control, working memory, and multisensory attention in chronic TBI patients and controls.

papers.title: Differences in brain responses to letter-sound and animal-sound in Arabic-speaking children learning to read.
papers.reason: The paper appears to focus on reading-related auditory and language processing rather than executive function, cognitive modelling, or impairment assessment.

papers.title: Higher Shifting Ability Is Associated with Reduced Threat-Safety Differentiation During Fear Generalization.
papers.reason: The paper relates cognitive shifting ability, an executive function component, to threat-safety differentiation during fear generalization, but executive-function modelling is not its central contribution.

papers.title: Neural correlates of inhibitory control and contributions of value-driven attentional capture in early childhood.
papers.reason: The paper directly studies fMRI and behavioural correlates of inhibitory control and value-driven attentional capture in children using a Go/No-Go paradigm.

papers.title: Characteristics of Dynamic Brain Network Revealed by fNIRS Based on Multitasking in Subjects With Mild Cognitive Impairment.
papers.reason: The paper studies dynamic brain networks during multitasking in people with mild cognitive impairment using fNIRS, making it relevant to executive-function assessment and neural mechanisms.

papers.title: Multi-frequency directed connectivity reveals ventral-stream and insular contributions to inhibitory control
papers.reason: The paper appears to report neural directed-connectivity findings about inhibitory control, a core executive function relevant to computational models of cognitive control.

papers.title: Neural correlates of executive functioning among adolescents and young adults living with HIV: a systematic review of structural and functional imaging studies
papers.reason: This systematic review directly links neuroimaging alterations to executive-function deficits including working memory, inhibitory control, and cognitive flexibility in a clinical human population.
